details: CONFIRMED by reading: lib/relay_gate.py run() sends stdout/stderr of the command to a file under the git dir, so nothing
bin/ci prints reaches the caller during the run; lib/relay_ci.py plugin_evals() prints the estimate only after the free
steps, and `bin/paid-cost guard eval` prints only on refusal (ran it: no output, rc 0). `bin/paid-cost today` exists and
prints the day's spend, so the information is at hand. The worker's report says "bin/ci already prints the estimate and the
day's spend", which is not so for the spend, and not "first" for either under relay gate.
evidence: $ python3 bin/paid-cost estimate  -> mean $10.53, max $21.41 over 21 stored runs
$ python3 bin/paid-cost today     -> 2026-10-27: spent $56.13 of the $200 cap, 3 runs
$ python3 bin/paid-cost guard eval; echo rc=$?  -> (no output) rc=0
lib/relay_ci.py:411: self.say("plugin evals: estimate %s; -j %s, ceiling $%s ..."), after the six free steps
failing_case: relay gate -C <wt> --paid on relay. The queue item's pass case: "the paid steps run only with an explicit flag (for example
--paid) and print their estimate and the day's spend first". Now: relay gate prints nothing until the whole gate ends (the
command's output goes to <git dir>/relay-gate.out, run() line ~290); bin/ci prints its "plugin evals: estimate ..." line
only into that file, after ~15 minutes of free steps, and never prints the day's spend (paid-cost guard is silent when it
passes). The person sees the cost only in the final log, after the money is spent.
Should: before the gate starts, relay gate --paid prints (stderr) the estimate and the day's spend, e.g.
"paid: mean $10.53, max $21.41 over 21 stored runs; 2026-10-27: spent $56.13 of the $200 cap, 3 runs".
fix_hint: In cmd_gate, when paid: if <worktree>/bin/paid-cost exists, run it with "estimate" and "today" (subprocess list args,
timeout=) and print both lines to stderr before relay_gate.run. Test with a fake bin/paid-cost in the fixture.
pass_cases: 1. relay gate --paid in a fixture whose bin/paid-cost prints "EST" for estimate and "SPENT" for today: stderr holds both
lines, and they appear before the gate command runs (the fake gate writes a marker; the lines precede it / are printed
while the marker does not yet exist).
2. relay gate (plain) in the same fixture: neither line is printed; the gate command gets --quick.
3. relay gate --paid in a project with no bin/paid-cost: the gate runs, no error, no cost line (or one line saying no
estimate is known).
4. relay gate -- --other: no cost lines, the command gets --other (as today).
reason: tests/test_gate_quick.py:74 passes, fails at base; plain/no-tool cases at :85, :92.

details: CONFIRMED: lib/relay_gate.py run() builds `shlex.split(binding(worktree)) + list(args)`, and cmd_gate now always adds
["--quick"] when no -- args are given. make and argparse both exit 2 on an unknown --quick (ran both). Measured today: the
two kit.toml files on this machine (relay, kartoteka) both use bin/ci, and relay's templates/bin-ci and kartoteka's bin/ci
ignore their arguments, so nothing breaks yet; the break comes with the first project whose gate.ci is make, npm, pytest or
any argparse script. The mode is relay-specific (only relay's gate has paid steps) but the default is applied to every
evidence: $ make ci --quick   -> make: unrecognized option `--quick'  rc=2
plugins/core/README.md:199: | gate.ci | required | the full gate; prints only what needs attention | "bin/ci" |
failing_case: A project with .relay/ and .claude/kit.toml [gate] ci = "make ci" (or a Python script with argparse, or pytest). relay gate
-C <wt> now runs `make ci --quick` -> "make: unrecognized option `--quick'", exit 2: the gate is red on every plain run and
the merge is refused, though the code is green. The gate.ci contract (plugins/core/README.md:199 "the full gate; prints
only what needs attention") never required the command to accept --quick; only relay's own bin/ci knows it.
Should: a plain relay gate runs the project's free gate in a way that works for a gate.ci that takes no arguments, e.g.
`make ci` exactly, and still `bin/ci --quick` for relay.
fix_hint: Name the free mode in the binding instead of in relay gate: an optional kit.toml key (e.g. gate.quick = "--quick", or
gate.ci_quick = "bin/ci --quick") that relay's own kit.toml sets; a plain relay gate adds it when present and nothing when
absent; --paid runs gate.ci alone. Document the key beside gate.ci in plugins/core/README.md.
pass_cases: 1. Fixture with kit.toml ci = "<script that exits 2 on any argument>": plain relay gate exits 0, log line 2 is
"cmd <script>" with no --quick.
2. relay's own setup (bin/ci, or a kit.toml binding that names the quick mode): plain relay gate runs bin/ci --quick
(log "cmd bin/ci --quick"), as the new test asserts today.
3. relay gate --paid on relay runs bin/ci with no argument.
4. relay gate -- --other passes --other unchanged in both setups.
reason: tests/test_gate_quick.py:35, :43, :49, :55 pass; :35 fails at base; README.md:200 documents gate.ci_quick.
findings.summary: a plain relay gate appends --quick to any project's gate.ci, so a gate command that rejects unknown options goes red
